domain: Why the widely accepted claim that 'grit' predicts long-term success survives despite the collapse of its standard evidentiary defenses
topic: Why the widely accepted claim that 'grit' predicts long-term success survives despite the collapse of its standard evidentiary defenses

source.title: Who do you think you are? There are two answers

movement.gist: Stage the popular belief: persistence and hard work, more than talent, explain who succeeds — introduced via the familiar 'grit' story used in schools, sports, and self-help, stated as something almost everyone accepts and the essay itself will not deny.

Separate out the bad reasons commonly offered: cherry-picked anecdotes of famous strivers, small non-replicating studies, and definitions of grit that quietly redefine themselves to fit whoever succeeded; show these arguments collapsing under scrutiny.

Insist the conclusion can nonetheless survive: independent lines of evidence — on habit formation, delayed gratification, and long-run skill acquisition — might support a modest version of the claim even after the popular arguments are discarded.

Pose the corruption question directly: if a true-seeming belief was adopted, taught, and institutionalized almost entirely through bad arguments, does its truth remain intact, or has something about our right to hold it been damaged — and what residue of doubt should remain even in the best surviving version of the claim.

primary.axis: whether the truth of a belief depends on the soundness of the arguments ordinarily given for it
poles: a conclusion can stand independent of its popular defenses
a conclusion inherits the epistemic damage of the reasoning used to support it

secondary.axis: perseverance as a real disposition vs. perseverance as a retrospective label applied to success
poles: grit is a measurable trait with predictive force
grit is a narrative imposed after outcomes are known

tension_system.interaction: the secondary tension supplies the case study through which the primary, more abstract question about belief-corruption gets tested and ultimately left unsettled

family_realization.note: Passage perfectly realizes 'Coalition of Errors': agrees modest-claim survives (para 3: 'quieter cousin... survives') while demolishing defenses (para 2: cherry-picked heroes, failed replications, definition-bending). The residue puzzle (para 4) directly asks: does truth clean bad-reasoning's record? Difficulty achieved through genuine tension between two instincts author refuses to settle.

ending_behavior.note: Closing performs 'The Residue' with perfect aperture-widening. 'What remains... is a residue of unearned confidence' states precisely what survives the best account: not whether belief is true, but whether confidence's magnitude is earned. 'I cannot settle which instinct is right' suspends refusal, not resolves it.

voice_consistency.note: 'The tribe assembles,' 'the elders cite,' 'ritual redescribes,' 'promotion rites of institutions' — institutional anthropology throughout. Phrases like 'wear the same name' and 'carrying the totem' treat familiar institutions (schools, offices, promotions) as alien ritual sites. Never lapses into generic essayist register.

distractor_efficiency.note: Q1(C): scope_inflation trap—treats opening statement as endorsement. Q2(D): example_promotion—survivor-bias flaw misread as refutation. Q3(B): half_truth—modest weight overstated to full justification. Q4(C): causal_inversion—independent work misread as doctrine-correction. Q5(A/D): false symmetries—both miss the acquisition→holding link. Each catches readers who miss passage's refusal to settle.

explanation_quality.note: Wrong-option notes cite exact passage locations and mechanism names: 'stance_misread' (author explicitly names two instincts), 'survivorship_bias' (cherry-picked heroes), 'definition-bending' (stubborn/grit flexing), 'causal_inversion' (independent work uninterested in totem). Never uses 'too extreme' or 'not mentioned.' Tied to specific text.

answers.reasoning: Passage ends on unresolved doubt about earned confidence despite possible truth.
Question highlights survivorship bias in citing only successful strivers.
Text explicitly says it supports 'something smaller and duller,' not the grand claim.
Failures discredit original defense; surviving research licenses only modest version.
The puzzle assumes acquisition process affects how responsibly a true belief is held.
Author explicitly says 'I cannot settle which instinct is right,' dwelling on residue of doubt.
